title: Blackballed along the Florida coast, deciding to leave for Jersey City
summary: The group is dated to 1948, tried in Hallandale, then fired under pressure on the owner's liquor license, so Sam calls his father in Jersey City.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: 1948--something like that. So--so we went to a--just 20 miles up the road, a town called Hallandale.

We went in there and I sounded a guy for a job. The guy said, "you the--that--that group that's playing at the Harlem Square?" We said "yes." He said, "yeah, man, sure." He said, "yeah, man, I'd be glad to have you." Said, "when can you start?" So we said, "anytime you want us to start there, we can start," you know.

And so we started playing. We came to work one night, man. And the guy looked at us and said, "man, I'm going to have to let ya'll go." I said, "what you talking about?" He said, "if I don't let you all -- if I don't fire you all--let ya'll go--they're going to take my liquor license, man."

They had--like I said, his brother was the head of the--they had black-balled us all over the whole coast. We couldn't play nowhere now. They black-balled us. The whole coast. And I said, well, it's time for me--to leave Florida. My father lives in Jersey City. So I call my father up and told him I got to get out of here now. I'm through with it.
